sources.entry: StartOS - Browser-based, graphical Operating System (OS) that makes running a personal server as easy as running a personal computer. (Source Code) MIT Rust

summary.one_liner: Start Technologies is the monorepo for Start9's products, flagship StartOS, a browser-managed Linux distribution for running a personal server.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a monorepo holding StartOS (the server OS, handling discovery, installation, network configuration, data backup, dependency management, and health monitoring of self-hosted services), start-cli (CLI for managing servers and registries and building .s9pk packages), start-registry (package registry API and asset server), StartTunnel (VPN/forwarding server), StartWRT (OpenWrt-based router OS for a SpaceMiT K1 board), the Start SDK for building service packages, and the marketplace and docs sites. The Rust backend lives in a shared start-core library, with an Angular web UI and a Node.js container runtime using LXC. Services run in isolated LXC containers and are packaged as S9PKs, a signed, merkle-archived format supporting partial downloads and verification. The README lists example services available on the Start9 Marketplace, including Bitcoin and Lightning nodes, Matrix, Nextcloud and Vaultwarden.
use_cases: run a personal server at home
replace cloud storage with self-hosted apps
install self-hosted services through a web interface
package an app as a StartOS service
set up a self-hosted VPN or reverse proxy with StartTunnel
flash OpenWrt-based router firmware with StartWRT
how_to_run: See AGENTS.md for the shared toolchain and development workflow
See projects/start-os/AGENTS.md to build a StartOS image
notable: Monorepo covering the whole Start9 stack, with StartOS as the flagship product
Services run in isolated LXC containers and are packaged as signed, merkle-archived S9PK files
Patch-DB, a diff-based reactive state store used for state synchronization
Includes StartTunnel for public addressing and port forwarding, and StartWRT for routers
Services are community-added through a marketplace and registry
caveats: Build-from-source instructions are delegated to AGENTS.md files and no explicit install commands are given in the README
StartWRT ships as a flashable image specifically for the SpaceMiT K1 hardware
Buying a pre-built Start9 server is presented as the easiest path
